scoring_note: Weights are our transcription of the public classic-format scoring rules. Sites change rules; every weight we used is in this payload, so check it against your contest before you trust it.

salaries.note: Salaries come from you. We do not scrape or republish any site's salary feed. Paste the CSV your contest site exports, or type a handful of prices in by hand; both stay in your browser.

notes: Skill projections (K, BB, HR, hits, innings, plate appearances) come from the rest-of-season engine behind the Redraft board. Nothing new is fit here.
Per-game playing time, the matchup multiplier and the park leg are display layer estimates with published league anchors. Each row lists them in `est`.
Relievers are not on the slate. Save and hold chances are not knowable before first pitch, and pretending otherwise would be the least honest number on the page.

Park factors are the Savant runs index the free-agent engine already builds, the same table the betting model prices games with. Savant's three-season table covers 29 of 30 parks; the thirtieth (the Athletics in Sacramento) and the Rays' Tropicana Field, back after a season away, have less than three seasons of data and are pulled toward neutral by their own samples. A factor applies only when the game is at the home club's own park; every other venue stays neutral and each row says which it got.
Games that had started, finished or been postponed when the board was built are left off it, because nobody can still draft them.

The matchup multiplier is the inverse of an innings-weighted opponent pitching index (5.4 of 9 innings to the announced starter's SEM+, the rest to the bullpen's Bullpen+), clamped. It mirrors the opponent term the streamer board has always used. It is a display heuristic, not a fitted run-environment model, and no backtest stands behind it yet.

Vegas implied team totals are read from odds snapshots the betting module already pays for, never fetched here. They are context to read beside a projection: no line on this page is priced off the market, and a game with no cached snapshot shows no total rather than an estimated one.

A lineup spot appears only once the club posts its card, which is usually after this board is built. Until then a hitter carries our projected start rate. Batting order is shown and is never paid into the projection.

slate_filter.policy: DRAFTABLE ONLY. A game that has started, finished, been postponed, suspended or cancelled is off the board and out of the optimizer pool; it is listed in excluded_games with the state the StatsAPI schedule reported.
slate_filter.on_unreadable: a game whose state cannot be read stays on the board

roster_filter.policy: FILTERED. A DFS pool is a set of players you can draft for tonight, and one who is not on an active roster cannot score. fantasy.json flags the same players instead, because a rest-of-season board is where you need to see them.
roster_filter.on_failure: a roster walk covering fewer than 28 of 30 clubs removes nothing; a player whose mlbam cannot be read is kept
